jobs.description: Adjunct Faculty - Citadel's Department of History (pooled position) History Adjunct Faculty View favorites Job Responsibilities: The Citadel, The Military College of South Carolina is currently accepting applications for The Citadel's History Department, to establish a pool for adjunct faculty assignments. Adjunct assignments may be temporary, part-time and/or on-call and may be immediate or as needed. This job posting is not for a specific assignment or for a full-time faculty position, but rather for a pool of candidates who may be considered for part-time teaching or allied faculty assignments. Duties may include teaching undergraduate courses or online graduate courses in American History, European History, Military and Diplomatic History, Non-Western History or World Geography. Undergraduate courses are offered during the day in face-to-face or hyflex formats throughout the academic year (fall, spring, and summer); Graduate Courses are offered in the evening or online. All adjunct positions are part-time, temporary, and per session appointments. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Abiding by and upholding the Citadel’s mission, policies, and core values. Utilizing effective teaching and learning practices such as presentations, demonstrations, class discussion, and other appropriate modes of instructional delivery; preparing course outlines and syllabi in accordance with program standards and in collaboration with the program coordinator. Completing student assessments required for program completion; hosting weekly office hours; meeting all scheduled class periods. Being available to students for individual consultation; submitting midterm grades for Corps students; recording class absences for Corps students and submitting final grades by the specified due date. The Citadel requires faculty to submit midterm grades for undergraduate students. The Citadel requires faculty to use the Attendance and Class Absence System to document class attendance for undergraduate students. Minimum Qualifications: A Master’s Degree in History is required to teach undergraduate history courses and a Master’s Degree in Geography is required to teach undergraduate geography courses. A PhD in History is required to teach graduate history courses and a PhD in Geography is required to teach graduate geography courses. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Exceptional interpersonal and collaboration skills. Experience in designing courses and materials for face-to-face and online formats.

Duties involve teaching undergraduate engineering courses to cadet, veteran, active duty, and civilian students in civil and construction engineering degree programs. Minimum Qualifications: Applicants should have an earned Master's or Doctorate degree in civil engineering, construction engineering, or a related academic field; with a minimum of 18 credit hours completed in graduate-level engineering curriculum related to technical subject matter area of course taught. Founded in 1842, The Citadel has a rich history and educational reputation. With our current location on the banks of the Ashley River in downtown Charleston, you are close to great restaurants, shopping and much more. There are about 2,300 undergraduate students who make up the South Carolina Corps of Cadets. Out of the Corps of Cadets, 1 out of 3 graduates earn a military commission. Students can choose from 31 Majors, 57 Minors, pre-health professions, and pre-law (a concentration in political science). The 11:1 student-to-faculty ratio guarantees students a quality education. Another 1,000 students attend the Graduate College, evening and online programs.

About the Institution The Citadel, also known as the Military College of South Carolina, is a public senior military college located in Charleston, South Carolina. Founded in 1842, The Citadel has a rich history and a heritage of excellence in education, emphasizing leadership development. The Citadel provides a unique, residential undergraduate experience in a military-college setting. There are approximately 2,300 undergraduate students who make up the South Carolina Corps of Cadets. Nearly one-third of our SCCC graduates earn a military commission in one of the five US Military Branches. Students can choose from 31 Majors and 57 Minors. The 11:1 student-to-faculty ratio guarantees students a quality education. Another 1,000 students, including MBA students, attend programs in the nonresidential Citadel Graduate College. The Citadel is located on the banks of the Ashley River near downtown Charleston, and is close to great restaurants and shopping, and much more. Life on The Citadel’s campus is the best way to work in Charleston. Stop into the full-service Starbucks on campus before the day begins. Between the parade deck (Summerall Field) and Hampton Park, right next to campus, one has access to the largest amount of green space on the peninsula.

jobs.description: Adjunct Faculty in Fine Arts - Citadel's Department of English, Fine Arts, and Communications (pooled position) English Fine Arts and Comm Adjunct Faculty Unclassified View favorites Job Responsibilities: The Citadel, The Military College of South Carolina is currently accepting applications to establish a pool for adjunct faculty assignments. Adjunct assignments may be temporary, part-time and/or on-call and may be immediate or as needed. This job posting is not for a specific assignment or for a full-time faculty position, but rather for a pool of candidates who may be considered for part-time teaching or allied faculty assignments. The Citadel’s Department of English, Fine Arts, and Communications is establishing a pool of applicants in the Fine Arts. Duties include teaching undergraduate course(s) in one or more of the following areas: Theatre, Cultural Preservation, 3-D Technologies, Photography, Photoshop, Forensic Photography, or other Fine Arts disciplines, based on departmental needs. Undergraduate courses are offered during the day in face-to-face or hyflex formats throughout the academic year (fall, spring, and summer). All adjunct positions are part-time, temporary, and per session appointments. jobs.description: Adjunct Faculty, Human Resources Management Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Please see Special Instructions for more details. Applications will be reviewed as they are received and until position is filled.Successful applications should include:1. Curriculum vitae2. Graduate and undergraduate transcripts. (Unofficial transcripts are acceptable for the application; official transcripts will be required later for an offer of employment.)For more information, please contact:Dr. Joanna Jackson, ChairDepartment of Management and MarketingWinthrop Universityjacksonj@winthrop.edu Position Details Position Information Winthrop Position Title Adjunct Faculty, Human Resources Management Job Description The Department of Management & Marketing in Winthrop University’s College of Business and Technology invites applications for an Adjunct Faculty member to teach MGMT 323: Acquiring Talent. MGMT 323 introduces students to the talent acquisition process within organizations, including recruitment, selection, and compensation and benefits as they relate to attracting and acquiring talent. The course emphasizes the application of human resource management concepts to contemporary organizational practices. The ideal candidate will bring relevant academic and/or professional experience in human resources, talent acquisition, recruitment, or a related management field and demonstrate a commitment to engaging, student-centered instruction. Position Responsibilities Teach MGMT 323: Acquiring Talent in accordance with established course objectives and departmental expectations. Provide engaging, student-centered instruction on recruitment, selection, talent acquisition, and related compensation and benefits topics. Connect course concepts to current human resource management practices and real-world organizational challenges. Develop and deliver course materials, assignments, assessments, and learning activities that support achievement of course learning outcomes. Incorporate relevant professional examples, applied activities, and contemporary HR practices into the course when appropriate. Provide timely and constructive feedback to students and maintain appropriate communication with students throughout the semester. Teach undergraduate-level courses in Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and Revit within the Interior Design program Develop and deliver engaging course content that aligns with program and CIDA accreditation standards Support student success initiatives, providing timely feedback Maintain a collaborative and inclusive learning environment Participate in professional development to stay current with evolving technologies and industry practices Contribute to program growth through curriculum support and innovation The Department of Art, Design and Letters is located within the School of the Arts and comprised of exceptional multi-disciplined programs in art and interior design. Fully accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD) and the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA), it is housed in the Milliken Fine Arts Building. At 30,000 square feet, there are designated classrooms in ceramics, sculpture, photography, printmaking, digital media, painting, drawing, and interior design. Converse University is a private, coed liberal arts university. We believe that a diverse faculty and staff are essential to achieving academic excellence; thus, we strongly encourage applications form candidates from all racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds. Located in the Upstate region of South Carolina, Spartanburg is a city full of exiting attractions, beautiful scenery, historically significant sites, seven colleges, and friendly people. Spartanburg is South Carolina's melting pot, mixing Southern culture and hospitality with traditions and cultures of other countries. Spartanburg's ideal proximity to the North Carolina mountains, the South Carolina coast, and major cities such as Atlanta and Charlotte make Spartanburg an attractive place to live. Disclaimer: The preceding job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and entail duties and responsibilities of the work performed by employees within this classification. It may not contain a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees to do this job. Applicants must submit the following documentation: Cover letter Curriculum vitae (CV) or resume Portfolio of professional and/or teaching work (if available) Contact information for professional references All materials, excluding the application, should be saved in one PDF file and loaded to the application site. ESSENTIAL DUTIES/NON-ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Teaching: 80% Includes development and delivery of course content within NASAD standards, grading and feedback, maintaining office hours, documenting as required for NASAD and meeting all deadlines for grade entry as required by the Office of the Registrar. Service:10% Includes service to the department, school, and university. Creative Scholarship: 10% Includes professional involvement in the field JOB QUALIFICATIONS: The Interior Design program at Converse University is committed to fostering creativity, critical thinking, and technical expertise. Faculty work collaboratively to prepare students for dynamic careers in the built environment. jobs.title: Adjunct Instructor in Music
jobs.description: JOB DESCRIPTION The Wofford College Department of Music invites applications to establish a pool of qualified candidates to serve as adjunct instructors. Opportunities may include applied instruction in voice or instruments, or classroom teaching in music theory, music appreciation, or other departmental courses. Our current needs include applied instructors in brass and percussion, as well as an instructor for class piano. The music program at Wofford is in an exciting phase of growth with strong support from faculty and administration for its continued development and expansion. Instructors will be contacted as openings arise. EXPECTATIONS Adjunct instructors at Wofford College work with undergraduate students in applied or classroom settings. All instruction is conducted in person on the Wofford campus. Specific teaching assignments and responsibilities will vary depending on student enrollment and departmental needs. QUALIFICATIONS A master’s degree in music (MM, MA, or equivalent) is required. Demonstrated excellence as both a performer and teacher. Strong communication skills and a commitment to student success. College-level teaching experience is preferred. APPLICATION To be fully considered, please apply via the Wofford Careers Page and include the following: 1. Letter of interest 2. Curriculum vitae (CV) 3. Recordings of sample lessons and/or performances (for applied instructors) 4. Contact information for three professional references Selected candidates will be contacted for an interview (in person or via Zoom) and may be asked to provide a teaching demonstration. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis and kept on file for future consideration. ABOUT WOFFORD COLLEGE Wofford College , established in 1854, is a private liberal arts residential college located a few blocks north of downtown Spartanburg, South Carolina. Wofford offers 27 major fields of study to a student body of nearly 1,800 undergraduates and is nationally known for the strength of its academic program, outstanding faculty, and study abroad participation. Wofford is home to one of the nation’s 290 Phi Beta Kappa chapters. The college community supports 19 NCAA Division I athletics teams and numerous student organizations, including honor societies, professional organizations, faith-based organizations, Greek life, and club sports. SPARTANBURG, SOUTH CAROLINA Spartanburg is in upstate South Carolina, 30 miles east of Greenville, South Carolina, an hour from Charlotte, North Carolina, and three hours east of Atlanta, Georgia. Historic Charleston and the South Carolina coast are three hours away, and Wofford sits an hour south of the artistic, culinary hub of Asheville, North Carolina. Spartanburg is a growing, diverse community that supports six colleges and universities, as well as numerous civic arts and cultural EEO STATEMENT Wofford College values diversity within our students, faculty and staff and strives to recruit, develop and retain the most talented people. Wofford College does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, transgender status, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws. For information about Wofford’s Title IX compliance, visit wofford.edu/administration/title-ix. It is the policy of Wofford College to provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities for employment. If you require any accommodations to participate in any part of the hiring process, please contact HumanResources@Wofford.edu.

jobs.title: Adjunct Instructor of English
jobs.description: Wofford College invites applications for adjunct instructors in the Department of English Language and Literature. We regularly need adjunct faculty to teach courses in the fall and spring semesters. Areas of need are as follows: English 102: Seminar in Literature and Composition. An in-depth study of some topic in literature. Reading and discussion lead to written work and independent investigation. Objectives are to read critically, think analytically and communicate effectively. Students are required to write several papers, one of which includes documentation. The course should be taken in the first year. Instructors have oriented courses to “Magical Realism,” “Holocaust Film,” “Cyberpunk” and “Utopian and Dystopian Fiction.” Offered only in the spring semester. English 200: Introduction to Literary Study. A study of the genres of fiction, poetry and/or drama designed to develop the student’s ability to read literature with sensitivity and understanding and with a sense of literary tradition. Emphasis is on close reading of works from a variety of critical perspectives. This course meets a general education requirement for Wofford students, but does not serve as a prerequisite for the major or minor in English. Offered both fall and spring semesters. English 201: English Literature to 1800. A study of works representative of the major writers and periods from the Middle Ages through the 18th century, with emphasis on critical understanding of these works and on the influences that produced them. This course meets a general education requirement for Wofford students and is required of all students majoring or minoring in English. Offered both fall and spring semesters. English 202: English Literature since 1800. A study of works representative of the major writers and periods from the Romantic movement to the present, with emphasis on critical understanding of these works and on the influences that produced them. This course meets a general education requirement for Wofford students and can meet prerequisite requirements for students majoring or minoring in English. Offered both fall and spring semesters. English 203: Survey of American Literature. A study of works representative of major American writers from the Colonial Period to the present, with emphasis on critical understanding of these works and on the influences that produced them. This course meets a general education requirement for Wofford students and can meet prerequisite requirements for students majoring or minoring in English. Offered both fall and spring semesters. English 204: Survey of World Literature. A survey of literary texts from locales around the globe (outside Britain and the United States). Readings will include short stories, poems and a few select novels spanning Asia, South Asia, South America, Africa, the Caribbean, the Middle East and Europe. This course meets a general education requirement for Wofford students and can meet prerequisite requirements for students majoring or minoring in English. Offered both fall and spring semesters. English 205: Introduction to the Study of Film. An introduction to the study of film as a technology, industry, cultural artifact and art form. Students will learn how to analyze visual texts, employing formal elements, such as editing, camera work and sound, and exploring the different ways these techniques have been employed by filmmakers in Hollywood and across the globe. This course meets a general education requirement for Wofford students and can meet prerequisite requirements for students majoring or minoring in English. Offered both fall and spring semesters. QUALIFICATIONS: For appointment, an advanced degree in English (M.A., M.F.A., or Ph.D.) and evidence of college-level teaching experience are required. jobs.description: Assistant Professor - Department of Psychology Psychology Full Time Permanent - Faculty 70,000 View favorites The Department of Psychology at The Citadel invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Psychology (specialization is open, preference given to Experimental Psychology) to begin in August 2027. The successful candidate is expected to actively engage undergraduate students in their research program. Located in historic Charleston, South Carolina, The Citadel has been ranked for the past 8 years (by U.S. News and World Report) as the top public college in the South among master’s-granting institutions. The Citadel’s Psychology Department has long been recognized for supporting and advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion. Candidates that can speak to and add to this mission are strongly encouraged to apply. Position Responsibilities The position will primarily entail teaching undergraduate courses based on the candidate’s specialization and also will include teaching Research Methods at the graduate level for Master’s students enrolled in the School Psychology and Clinical Counseling programs. Preference will be given to candidates who can teach core courses in the undergraduate program (Introduction to Psychological Science, Psychological Statistics, Research Design/Experimental Psychology), along with elective courses in the candidate’s area of specialization (e.g., Social Psychology, Sports Psychology, Health Psychology, Neuroscience, etc.). Required Qualifications Minimum requirements include a doctorate in an experimental area of psychology or related discipline (ABD candidates will be considered), as well as demonstrated research potential and the willingness to maintain a productive research program that incorporates undergraduate students. Preference will be given to candidates who demonstrate evidence of teaching experience and instructional effectiveness at the post-secondary level. The Department of Psychology (with 11 full-time faculty) has approximately 75 undergraduate majors; additionally, we have approximately 100 graduate students between the two programs housed within the Department of Psychology – School Psychology and Clinical Counseling, both accredited (by NASP and MPCAC, respectively). The Citadel is a co-educational military college that provides a unique undergraduate learning environment complemented by a non-military Citadel Graduate College. jobs.description: Wofford College invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track assistant professor of finance to join its Department of Accounting, Business and Finance starting in Fall 2027. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Wofford prides itself in providing excellence in undergraduate teaching for its students, leading them to be well prepared for meaningful lives and rewarding vocations. Faculty expectations include: (1) teach three undergraduate class sections in each of the fall and spring semesters, as well as a January interim course (3-1-3), (2) advise students, (3) pursue active scholarship embodied in theory or practice, and (4) serve on college and departmental committees. A demonstrated record of superior undergraduate teaching is strongly preferred. QUALIFICATIONS: Candidates are expected to have earned a PhD in a relevant field by August 2027. Candidates with MS/MBA and significant, relevant professional experience will also be considered. In all cases, degrees must be earned from an accredited institution. APPLICATION: For consideration, please apply using the link provided, which will direct you to the Wofford College Careers page. Application materials may be uploaded as a single document or individually. Application materials include: Letter of interest Resume or curriculum vitae Statement of teaching philosophy Sample course evaluations Three letters of recommendation Applications must be submitted by September 30, 2026. Please contact Prof. Diane Farley farleyds@wofford.edu , with questions regarding this position. ABOUT WOFFORD COLLEGE Wofford College , established in 1854, is a private liberal arts residential college located a few blocks north of downtown Spartanburg, South Carolina. Wofford offers 27 major fields of study to a student body of nearly 1,800 undergraduates and is nationally known for the strength of its academic program, outstanding faculty, and study abroad participation. Wofford is home to one of the nation’s 290 Phi Beta Kappa chapters. The college community supports 19 NCAA Division I athletics teams and numerous student organizations, including honor societies, professional organizations, faith-based organizations, Greek life, and club sports. SPARTANBURG, SOUTH CAROLINA Spartanburg is located in upstate South Carolina, 30 miles east of Greenville, South Carolina, an hour from Charlotte, North Carolina, and three hours east of Atlanta, Georgia. Historic Charleston and the South Carolina coast are three hours away, and Wofford sits an hour south of the artistic, culinary hub of Asheville, North Carolina. Spartanburg is a growing, diverse community that supports six college and university campuses along with numerous civic arts and cultural associations. It became the first city in South Carolina to join the Government Alliance on Race and Equity and, in 2012, became one of five cities nationally to participate in the 10-year Wellville program, a national nonprofit initiative dedicated to improving equitable well-being in U.S. cities. jobs.description: Wofford College invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor of International Affairs to join its Department of Government and International Affairs starting in fall 2027. Wofford faculty are teacher-scholars with a high aptitude and interest in undergraduate teaching and advising, community outreach and a commitment to the liberal arts. At Wofford, faculty serve as teacher-scholars dedicated to the education and mentorship of undergraduates in a liberal arts tradition. Faculty earn tenure after six years by demonstrating excellence in teaching, continued scholarly development, participation in advising, and service to the REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Applicants will have: Earned a Ph.D. in Management, or closely related field, by August 2027. Candidates with MS/MBA and significant, relevant professional experience will also be considered. In all cases, degrees must be earned from an accredited institution Demonstrated commitment to excellence in in-person, undergraduate-level teaching. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience with in-person teaching of undergraduate students, Relevant industry experience, Excellent communication skills, Enthusiasm for advising undergraduate students, Commitment to teaching at a small, liberal arts college, and Ability to engage in scholarship embodied in theory or practice. EXPECTATIONS: Wofford faculty members are primarily educators committed to excellence in teaching. Faculty expectations include: Teaching - Faculty develop and practice effective, student-centered pedagogies to facilitate our students’ academic development. For humanities and social science faculty, a standard teaching load is 3-1-3, including a January term commonly referred to as Interim. Scholarship – Faculty engage in scholarship. Wofford embraces a broad definition of scholarship that includes discipline-specific, pedagogical and interdisciplinary research. Scholarship may include, but is not limited to, publication, obtaining and maintaining professional certification or licensure, engaging students in service learning, or participation in academic conferences. Advising - Faculty participate in the College’s advising program by advising students in both the general education curriculum as well as majors/minors in the faculty member’s discipline. Service – Faculty contribute to the mission of the College by participating in service opportunities which include, but are not limited to, faculty committee service. Faculty also support the institution by participating in faculty governance, departmental meetings, admissions events, and athletic events. APPLICATION: For consideration, please apply using the link provided, which will direct you to the Wofford College Careers page. Application materials may be uploaded as a single document or individually. Application materials include: Letter of interest Resume or curriculum vitae Statement of teaching philosophy Sample course evaluations Three letters of recommendation, at least one of which should be from someone who can speak to your prior teaching experience While we will continue to accept applications until the position is filled, applications received by October 15, 2026, are guaranteed consideration. Please contact Prof. Diane Farley farleyds@wofford.edu , with questions regarding this position. ABOUT WOFFORD COLLEGE Wofford College , established in 1854, is a private liberal arts residential college located a few blocks north of downtown Spartanburg, South Carolina. Wofford offers 27 major fields of study to a student body of nearly 1,800 undergraduates and is nationally known for the strength of its academic program, outstanding faculty, and study abroad participation. Wofford is home to one of the nation’s 290 Phi Beta Kappa chapters. The college community supports 19 NCAA Division I athletics teams and numerous student organizations, including honor societies, professional organizations, faith-based organizations, Greek life, and club sports. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Occupational Therapy (Pediatrics)
jobs.description: Assistant Professor of Occupational Therapy (Pediatrics) Position Description This is a full-time, twelve-month, non-tenure-track instructional faculty position that reports to the Program Director of the Occupational Therapy Doctoral Program in the School of Health Professions at Presbyterian College. This position will contribute the education, mentorship, and professional development of entry-level doctoral occupational therapy students. The faculty member will provide primary instructional expertise in pediatric occupational therapy while also contributing to curricular, experiential, and professional development needs of the program. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. The duties of the position are as follows: Pediatric Teaching Responsibilities Develop, coordinate, and teach pediatric occupational therapy content across the OTD curriculum, including pediatric evaluation, assessment, intervention, clinical reasoning, documentation, and evidence-based practice. Provide instruction addressing occupational performance, participation, and development across infancy, childhood, and adolescence, with consideration of physical, cognitive, psychosocial, sensory, developmental, and environmental factors. Integrate pediatric content across occupational therapy practice settings, including early intervention, schools, outpatient pediatrics, inpatient and rehabilitation settings, community-based programs, and other emerging areas of pediatric practice. Design and facilitate engaging classroom, laboratory, simulation, case-based, and experiential learning activities that promote clinical reasoning and application of occupational therapy theory to pediatric practice. Incorporate evidence-based pediatric assessment tools, intervention approaches, clinical documentation, outcome measures, and current professional standards into coursework. Teach students to analyze the relationship between child development, occupations, routines, environments, and participation in meaningful activities. Incorporate family-centered, occupation-centered, culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and developmentally appropriate approaches to pediatric occupational therapy practice. Prepare students to collaborate effectively with parents, caregivers, educators, healthcare providers, and other professionals involved in the care and support of children and families. Incorporate community-based pediatric learning experiences that allow students to apply classroom knowledge to authentic occupational therapy situations. This expectation aligns with the OTD program’s emphasis on experiential learning, community engagement, and service. Evaluate student learning through appropriately designed examinations, practical examinations, assignments, laboratory performance, presentations, clinical reasoning activities, and other assessment methods. Teaching Responsibilities Teach a course load appropriate to the discipline and position. Plan and organize instruction to maximize student learning objectives. Implement contemporary teaching and learning strategies to communicate subject matter to students. Modify, as needed, instructional approaches to address student diversity. Learn and use technology to enhance teaching and the educational experience. i.e. the internet, Institutional learning system (Blackboard etc.), distance coursework (tele-medicine /video conferencing as needed), and other interactive technology, as appropriate. Encourage and facilitate the development of communication skills and higher order thinking skills through appropriate assignments. Contribute to the selection and development of instructional materials in accordance with course objectives and the curricular design. Incorporate specific core competencies into specific coursework taught. Develop, update, and post course syllabi in a timely manner in accordance with program policies. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Political Science – U.S. Politics / Pre-Law Studies (Tenure-Track)
jobs.description: Assistant Professor of Political Science U.S. Politics / Pre-Law Studies (Tenure-Track) Position Description The Department of Political Science at Presbyterian College invites applications for a 9-month, tenure-track, assistant professor position in U.S. politics. (The Ph.D. in political science is strongly preferred, but ABD will be considered at the rank of instructor.) The successful candidate will also serve as Director of Pre-law Studies, with a start date of August 16, 2027. Review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. The Department of Political Science is one of the largest on campus, as it typically graduates around 15-20 students each year. External observers highlight small class sizes, a well-developed curriculum, and a faculty committed to student learning and success. In that context, successful applicants should display a strong enthusiasm for teaching and a commitment to both service and scholarship. Responsibilities Responsibilities for this position include teaching in the Pre-Law minor, including two courses in constitutional law (governmental powers, and civil rights/liberties) as well as a course in legal studies. The ideal candidate will also teach an introductory course in U.S. government as well as upper-level courses in U.S. politics or public policy, with an open field of specialization. The teaching load is seven courses per academic year (4:3). In addition to teaching, responsibilities as Director of Pre-Law Studies include coordination of the College’s established pre-law program, advising Pre-Law minors and other students interested in law, and networking with law schools and other graduate programs, including opportunities in political science, public administration, or state and local politics. The ideal candidate will also contribute to student-focused activities, including the Pre-Law and Political Science clubs, South Carolina Student Legislature, and various on-campus events. To Apply Submission of application materials by electronic mail is strongly encouraged. Interested individuals should provide, at a minimum, a letter stating interest in the position, a curriculum vitae, transcripts from undergraduate and graduate institutions, and three letters of recommendation. Materials should be sent to the Office of the Provost at provost@presby.edu. For individual questions, please contact Dr. David Liu, chair of the Department of Political Science, at zliu@presby.edu. About Presbyterian College Presbyterian College (PC) is a liberal arts college affiliated with the Presbyterian Church USA. The college is committed to an equitable and inclusive learning environment for all students, supports academic freedom, and encourages community involvement. Located in Clinton, South Carolina, PC is approximately 40 minutes from Greenville and Spartanburg, South Carolina and about one hour from Columbia, South Carolina. The region offers abundant opportunity for social and recreational activities, with easy access to Asheville and Charlotte, North Carolina, and Atlanta, Georgia. Presbyterian College is an EEO employer and does not discriminate against any person or group on the basis of age, color, disability, gender, pregnancy, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status or genetic information. PC is building a culturally diverse faculty and staff committed to working in a multicultural environment and encourages applications from minorities and women. Job Title: Assistant Professor of Sociology Job Family: Furman Faculty Full-Time/Part-Time: Full time Pay Type: Salary Department: Sociology Job Summary: The Department of Sociology at Furman University invites applications for two Assistant/Associate/Professor tenure-track positions beginning August 1, 2027. We welcome candidates from any substantive area of sociology whose expertise complements and expands our existing departmental strengths, and whose work reflects a commitment to rigorous inquiry and meaningful engagement with students. A Ph.D. in Sociology is required by August 1, 2027. Job Description: We encourage applications from candidates who demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching, student mentorship, and research in a liberal arts environment. The teaching responsibility is five courses per academic year. A strong application will articulate how the candidate envisions contributing to our core curriculum, which includes Introduction to Sociology, Sociological Theory, Qualitative and Quantitative Methods, and 200-level courses in the Sociology of Gender and Sexuality, Race/Ethnicity, or Social Class. Beyond core requirements, we welcome applicants who would bring new course offerings that deepen and diversify our curricular landscape and contribute to the goals of Furman University’s Strategic Plan. Applicants should submit the following documents in a single PDF in the order listed: a letter of interest, C.V., statement of teaching philosophy, and complete contact information for three references. The statement of teaching philosophy should describe your inclusive teaching and mentoring efforts, broadly conceived, and how your teaching and mentoring may contribute to a liberal arts and sciences community that aims, among other things, to “honor inquiry, promote diversity, [and] strive for equity” ( FUture Focused ) . You may also discuss any relevant professional development, service contributions, or other experiences that have refined your skills or demonstrate your efforts in these areas. Additional materials may be requested at later stages of the search process for candidates who advance. Furman University is dedicated to fostering a vibrant and inclusive community through excellence in teaching, mentorship, and programming. We believe that cultural understanding, inclusiveness, and freedom of inquiry, thought, and discourse are essential components of a transformative undergraduate education. jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Accounting
jobs.description: The College of Business and Economics at Anderson University cordially invites applications for a professional-track, ten-month instructional position in Accounting at the rank of Assistant Professor. The preferred start date for the position is Spring 2027. A Master’s degree or higher in Accounting, or a Master’s degree in a related discipline with at least 18 graduate credit hours in Accounting, is required. Preference will be given to those who have a CPA with a record of successful teaching at the undergraduate or graduate level. In addition, work experience within the field is also preferred, though not required. Exceptionally well-qualified candidates with teaching and industry related experience will be considered for appointment at an advanced rank (associate or full professor). We are seeking a faculty member who can support the successful growth of the Accounting program within the College of Business and Economics. Classes primarily focus on Financial Accounting and Managerial Accounting. While most classes taught will be in-seat to undergraduate students, faculty could have a potential teaching schedule that includes undergraduate and graduate classes offered at the Anderson main campus, the Greenville campus, and/or online. Anderson University is an innovative, entrepreneurial, premier comprehensive liberal arts university affiliated with the South Carolina Baptist Convention. The University seeks candidates with a strong Christian value system, lifestyle, and commitment to the integration of faith and learning. The College of Business and Economics at Anderson University is ACBSP accredited, has 20 full-time faculty members, serves approximately 500 graduate and undergraduate students, offers eight majors in the BSB degree program, six concentrations in the BBA degree program, a Bachelor of Organizational Leadership degree program, and fourteen minors. In addition, our graduate program includes an MOL, an MBA with four concentrations, and several certificate offerings. Anderson University is a “more selective” comprehensive Christian university. The institution has degree programs at the bachelor, masters, and doctoral levels, both on campus and online. Anderson University is among US News and World Report’s “Best Regional Universities South,” and is on the publication’s “Most Innovative,” “Best Value,” “Best Undergraduate Teaching,” “Best Social Mobility” and “Best Online Programs” lists. Anderson is also highly ranked nationally for Student Engagement by the Wall Street Journal; is a “Best College” among institutions of higher learning in the southeast by The Princeton Review; and is an Apple Distinguished School. More information about the AU College of Business and Economics is available at https://www.andersonuniversity.edu/academics/business About our Commitment to Fairness in Employment Anderson University does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, sex, disability, age, religion, genetic information, veteran or military status, or any other basis on which the University is prohibited from discrimination under the local, state, or federal law, in its employment or in the provision of its services, including but not limited to its programs and activities, admissions, educational policies, scholarship and loan programs, and athletic and other University-administered programs. As a Christian institution of higher education, Anderson University is entitled to certain religious accommodations under federal and state law, including Title IX of the Education Amendments Act and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. For questions or concerns contact the Office of Human Resources at hr@andersonuniversity.edu .

jobs.title: Doctor of Medical Science Adjunct
jobs.description: college of health science The College of Health Science at North Greenville University is accepting applications for an adjunct faculty member to develop and teach Advanced Pharmacology within the Doctor of Medical Science (DMSc) program. The DMSc is a fully online doctoral program designed for practicing healthcare professionals seeking advanced education in clinical practice, leadership, education, and evidence-based healthcare. Advanced Pharmacology is a 3 credit hour doctoral course examining contemporary issues and emerging developments in pharmacology, with an emphasis on the evaluation and application of pharmacologic information in clinical practice. Major areas of study include medication optimization, polypharmacy, deprescribing, individualized pharmacotherapy, medication safety, pharmacogenomics, emerging therapies, and critical evaluation of pharmacologic literature. The successful candidate will possess advanced expertise in pharmacology and will be responsible for developing and delivering academically rigorous, clinically relevant course content appropriate for doctoral-level healthcare professionals. The course is delivered fully online through the University's Canvas learning management system. RESPONSIBILITIES: The adjunct faculty member will be responsible for the development, delivery, and assessment of the Advanced Pharmacology course. Responsibilities include: Design and develop an eight-week, three-credit-hour graduate course in Advanced Pharmacology in collaboration with DMSc program leadership. Create weekly instructional materials, including recorded lectures, presentations, readings, learning activities, and other appropriate educational resources. Develop meaningful assignments and assessments that require students to evaluate, synthesize, and apply contemporary pharmacologic evidence to clinical practice. Provide timely, substantive, and constructive feedback on student assignments and academic work. Maintain regular and meaningful engagement with students throughout the course. Guide students in the critical evaluation and interpretation of pharmacologic literature, including assessment of medication efficacy, safety, clinical relevance, and applicability to patient care. Physical Requirements Mobility: Able to move between buildings and attend classes, meetings, and functions across campus. Speaking: Frequently convey detailed or important instructions and ideas accurately, professionally, and with a contextually appropriate tone and volume. Cognitive/Emotional: Ability to critically think and express emotions and thoughts in an honest, collegial, constructive, and prudent manner. TRAVEL Adjunct faculty in the DMSc program are remote employees and are not required to travel to campus. WORKING RELATIONSHIPS and SCHEDULE The adjunct faculty member will work closely with and report to the Program Director of the Doctor of Medical Science program within the College of Health Sciences. The Advanced Pharmacology course is delivered fully online in an asynchronous format. Although there are no on-campus teaching requirements, adjunct faculty are expected to maintain consistent availability and communication throughout the course, engage regularly with students, provide timely feedback, and meet all established program and University deadlines. Course development will occur in coordination with DMSc program leadership prior to the course offering. Because pharmacology is a rapidly evolving discipline, the faculty member will also be expected to maintain and update course materials to ensure that instruction reflects contemporary evidence and clinical practice.

jobs.title: Instructor of Dance
jobs.description: Instructor of Dance Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Posting Details POSTING INFORMATION Internal Title Instructor of Dance Position Type Instructor School/Area School of the Arts Department Theatre & Dance Position Description Full-time Instructor of Dance, Non-Tenure-TrackCOLLEGE OF CHARLESTON is accepting applications for a full-time, nine-month, non-tenure track appointment in the Department of Theatre and Dance. This appointment begins January 1, 2027. This is a full-time permanent position with a teaching load of four courses per semester. In the sixth year, the Instructor undergoes review for promotion to Senior Instructor. The Department of Theatre and Dance is NAST-accredited, offering BA and MAT degrees in Theatre and a BA in Dance. We seek a candidate who can inspire both beginning and experienced students in their initial dance studies and actively support the ongoing development of the Dance major. Regularly taught courses will serve as an entry point to dance students new to the department and those completing General Education requirements. The ideal candidate will bring expertise in one or more areas of dance technique, as well as the ability to teach non-Western dance practices, somatics, and/or theory-based courses. Responsibilities include teaching a full course load each semester (4/4); providing service to the department through recruitment efforts and serving on departmental committees; maintaining a record of professional development and sustained pedagogy; serving as an academic advisor to dance majors; guiding and assisting student participation in various conferences and festivals; and potentially choreographing for department productions as needed. Qualifications:MA, MFA, or PhD required by January 1, 2027; Professional experience/scholarship in dance; Prior undergraduate teaching experience strongly preferred. The ideal candidate is a dynamic educator passionate about mentoring students in a liberal arts program, possessing either an MFA or a PhD in Dance or a closely related discipline; has a minimum of three years’ experience teaching in post-secondary education; and has prior experience in student recruitment/advising/mentorship. Candidates who are currently active in and contributing to the dance field, either in traditional modes of scholarship or through creative practice, are preferred. Review of applications begins September 15, 2026. The College is located in historic downtown Charleston in a coastal metropolitan area of 750,000. Additional information about the institution and the surrounding area is available at https://www.cofc.edu/.The College of Charleston is a nationally recognized public liberal arts and sciences university located in the heart of historic Charleston, SC. Since our founding in 1770, we have maintained a strong liberal arts curriculum. The College is a state-supported, comprehensive institution and ranks among the nation’s top universities in providing quality education in the arts, sciences, education, and business. No other university has the unique combination of our exceptional faculty, diverse programs, historic campus, coastal location, modern facilities, and cutting-edge programs. The student body numbers over 11,000 students in undergraduate and graduate programs combined. Special Instructions to Applicants Posting Date 07/29/2026 Closing Date Open Until Filled? Yes Posting Number F2026008P EEO Statement The College of Charleston is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any individual or group on the basis of sex, gender (including gender identity and/or expression), pregnancy, race, religion, color, national origin, age, disability, military or veteran status, sexual orientation, genetic information, and other classifications protected by applicable federal, state, and local laws. jobs.title: Post Doctoral Fellow - Glenn Department of Civil Engineering
jobs.description: Clemson University: College of Engineering, Computing and Applied Sciences: Glenn Department of Civil Engineering Location LOWRY HALL (000024) BLDG000024 FL01 Open Date Sep 18, 2026 Description The postdoctoral researcher will conduct research focused on infrastructure system resilience, risk assessment, and data-driven modeling, with particular emphasis on transportation and rail infrastructure systems. The position will involve the development and application of system-level modeling and analytical approaches to evaluate infrastructure performance, vulnerability, risk, and resilience under natural hazards, climate-related stresses, and other disruptive events. The researcher will work with large and heterogeneous infrastructure, environmental, and climate datasets and develop computational and data-driven models to support resilience assessment and decision-making. The work may include the use and analysis of Global Climate Models (GCMs), statistically or dynamically downscaled climate projections, and other climate and hazard datasets to evaluate current and future risks to infrastructure systems. The postdoctoral researcher will also contribute to ongoing externally funded research projects, preparation of technical reports and peer-reviewed publications, development and implementation of computational models, coordination with research collaborators and project partners, and mentoring or supporting graduate and undergraduate researchers as appropriate. Qualifications Ph.D. in Civil Engineering, Transportation Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a closely related field. The Ph.D. must be completed by the appointment start date. Demonstrated experience in system-level modeling and analysis of infrastructure systems, particularly in the areas of risk, resilience, vulnerability, or reliability. Experience with data-driven modeling and quantitative/computational research methods. Experience working with Global Climate Models (GCMs), downscaled GCM products, climate projections, or related climate and hazard datasets. Strong analytical, programming, and technical communication skills. Ability to conduct independent research while working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team. Prior research experience involving rail or transportation infrastructure system resilience is preferred but not required. Application Instructions Please include C.V. Cover Letter, Letter of recommendation, and 3 contact references (one page). Application Process This institution is using Interfolio's Faculty Search to conduct this search. Applicants to this position receive a free Dossier account and can send all application materials, including confidential letters of recommendation, free of charge. Apply Now Equal Employment Opportunity Statement Clemson University is an EEO/AA employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to characteristics protected by applicable law including disability and protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Provost and Dean of the College
jobs.college: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
jobs.description: Provost and Dean of the College Provost and Dean of College Full Time Permanent - Faculty Full Time Permanent - Staff Unclassified View favorites PROVOST AND DEAN OF THE COLLEGE The Citadel, The Military College of South Carolina, seeks an accomplished academic leader to serve as Provost and Dean of the College. Reporting to the President, the Provost serves as the College's Chief Academic Officer, directing the Deans of the College's Schools and collaborating with the Commandant's office to align the academic and military components of a Citadel education. The Provost will also collaborate with the college’s other Vice Presidents as part of the President’s senior leadership team. Founded in 1842, The Citadel is one of the nation's senior military colleges, located on a 300-acre campus in Charleston, South Carolina. The College is home to the South Carolina Corps of Cadets, numbering approximately 2,300 students, as well as The Citadel Graduate College, which serves close to 1,000 students through evening, online, and graduate programs. The Citadel has been named the No. 1 public regional university in the South by U.S. News & World Report for 15 consecutive years, and the No. 1 public college for veterans in the South for eight years. Gen. Frank McKenzie, a 1979 Citadel graduate, began his tenure as the College's 21st President in July of this year. Academic programs are organized across the Tommy and Victoria Baker School of Business, the School of Engineering, the School of Humanities and Social Sciences, the Swain Family School of Science and Mathematics, the Zucker Family School of Education, and the Krause School for Leadership and Ethics, along with The Citadel Graduate College. The College maintains an 11:1 student-to-faculty ratio, and nearly all faculty hold a doctorate or the highest degree in their field. The successful candidate will bring a record of academic leadership, including experience with faculty affairs, curriculum, and accreditation, along with the ability to lead within a structured, values-driven military campus culture. Qualified candidates must hold an earned doctorate or terminal degree, possess scholarly credentials appropriate for a tenured appointment, and demonstrate a successful record of senior academic leadership at the dean level or higher. Experience with both a traditional undergraduate program and adult, graduate, or online education is preferred. Military experience is not necessary, but the Provost will wear a uniform and will hold the grade of Brigadier General in the South Carolina Militia (SCM). Applications, nominations, and inquiries should be directed to the search firm contact listed below. Review of candidates will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Interested parties are encouraged to submit their materials to our consultant at the address below by October 15, 2026, for full consideration. Application materials must include a current CV and letter of interest. The Citadel Provost and Dean of the College Search Funk Associates 2911 Turtle Creek Boulevard, Suite 300 Dallas, Texas 75219 Email: Krisha.Creal@funkassociates.com

jobs.description: Job Description Summary A cancer research laboratory under Dr. Jezabel Rodriguez-Blanco within the Hollings Cancer Center and the Darby Children’s Research Institute has an opening for a postdoctoral position. Entity Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC - Univ) Worker Type Employee Worker Sub-Type​ Research Grant Cost Center CC001013 COM PEDS Children's Research Institute CC Pay Rate Type Hourly, Salary Pay Grade University-00 Pay Range 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.000 Scheduled Weekly Hours 40 Work Shift Job Description This lab utilizes in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo models, including genetic mouse models and patient-derived orthotopic xenografts, to investigate the intracellular drivers of pediatric brain tumor growth. The primary research focus is on elucidating the signaling mechanisms that contribute to the relapse of medulloblastoma, the most common malignant pediatric brain tumor.
